classification.difficultyReason: Model three successive binary outcomes and count events involving all, exactly one and at least two.

content.prompt: A family has three children. Assume that each child is equally likely to be a boy or a girl, independently of the other children. By drawing a tree diagram that shows all the possible combinations of children, find the probability that:

answer.worked:
Let $G$ mean girl and $B$ mean boy, recording children in birth order. The shared tree has eight equally likely paths. Only $GGG$ has three girls.
$$P(\text{three girls})=\frac18$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: only one child is a boy

answer.worked:
The favourable paths are $BGG, GBG, GGB$, out of eight equally likely paths.
$$P(\text{only one boy})=\frac38$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: at least two of the children are girls

answer.worked:
The favourable paths are $GGG, GGB, GBG, BGG$, out of eight equally likely paths.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{at least two girls})&=\frac48\\P(\text{at least two girls})&=\frac12\end{align*}$$

spec.description: One shared three-stage binary tree, in birth order, with G for girl and B for boy.
spec.mathematics: Eight equally likely ordered outcomes: GGG, GGB, GBG, GBB, BGG, BGB, BBG, BBB.
